verdict.rationale: Statsig's docs say gates toggle product behavior "in real time" and can serve as an emergency disable switch that "immediately" turns off a code branch, so the kill-switch capability is first-party. However, nothing explains how changes reach connected SDKs (streaming vs. polling) or how fast. SDKs evaluating locally after initialization implies cached config whose refresh behavior is undocumented here. Missing for 10: documented streaming or polling propagation mechanism, stated propagation latency in seconds, SDK config refresh intervals, independent or hands-on confirmation that the kill switch takes effect promptly.

support.subject: As a developer, flag changes propagate to connected SDKs in seconds via streaming or fast polling — a kill switch actually kills

citations.quote: allow you to toggle the behavior of your product in real time without deploying new code
Have an emergency disable switch that lets you immediately turn off a particular code branch for users in production
